newsitem.title: GERMANY: German mobile phone price war heats up.
newsitem.headline: German mobile phone price war heats up.

text.p: The price war raging on Germany's mobile phone market flared up again on Thursday when two of the three main operators slashed call charges and eliminated some costly monthly fees.

German mobile phone operators Mannesmann Mobilfunk GmbH and E-Plus Mobilfunk GmbH both said they would scrap the minimum usage limit and lower connection fees while at the same time shorten the time alloted to each calling unit.

The changes to the billing structure were aimed at making it less expensive for short calls and to compete with Deutsche Telekom, which last month introduced a new mobile phone service with no basic monthly charge and simple billing.
Mannesmann, which operates the D2 digital cellular phone network, said it would scrap its 15 mark minimum usage and the 69 marks cancellation charge from February 24.

The D2 one-off connection fee would be halved to 49.95 marks and users of its D2-Fun24 and D2-Classic24 tariffs could receive billing down to the second for an additional charge of five marks and 8.25 marks a month respectively.
Previously, callers had to pay for the first entire minute regardless of how long the call lasted.
E-Plus said it would get rid of its minimum usage fee of 20 marks a month and halve its one-off connection charge to 49 marks. Cancellation fees would remain at 74.75 marks.
